**(1) First message to the user**

The framing holds. I checked `lib/notify.ts#post` and traced two callers: `jobs/report.ts`, which sends inline, and `jobs/digest.ts`, which relies on the default channel. Both paths use the same formatting and retry contract, and neither needs another loader or runtime dependency.

Here is what the code supports and what it does not:

- **`post` owns the shared send.** It builds the `[notice] ` text, hardcodes `channel: "general"`, and makes up to two attempts, rethrowing on the second failure (`lib/notify.ts:2-6`).
- **`report` duplicates that send.** It repeats the same body shape, the same endpoint and the same two-attempt loop. The only difference is that it uses its own `channel` parameter (`jobs/report.ts:1-6`).
- **`digest` depends on the default.** It calls `post("Daily digest")` with no channel, so it relies on the `general` default (`jobs/digest.ts:2`).
- **No claim was disproved or corrected.** "Retries" means one retry after the first failure, and the design keeps that exact count.
- **One fact is unverified.** I only have these three files, so I can't confirm that `digest` is the only importer of `post`. The design doesn't depend on that unless we make the channel argument required. In that case, it decides how many call sites change.

My assumption is that no new notification service is introduced. The shared helper already owns this path.

How should existing callers of `post` be treated when it learns to take a channel?
A) Add an optional channel argument that defaults to `general`, so existing calls stay untouched.
B) Make the channel argument required, and update every existing call to pass `general` explicitly.
C) other - name it
Recommendation: A - It reaches the requested channel and leaves the default-channel callers exactly as they are.

---

**(2) Approaches message**

No implicit dependency was found missing or uncheckable. Both caller paths and `post` itself were traced in primary code, and no loader or runtime dependency is involved beyond the shared endpoint they already use.

The two approaches differ on one question: who states the channel. Either `post` keeps owning the `general` default, or every caller must name its channel.

**Recommended: an optional channel on `post`, with report reusing it.** This is the reuse-only option. `post` is the shared path that nearly fits. It already owns formatting and the two-attempt retry, and it lacks only a caller-supplied channel. Adding `channel = "general"` as an optional second parameter closes that gap. `report` then drops its copied body and loop and calls `post(message, channel)`, so it inherits the owned retry contract. Its own `report(message, channel)` signature stays the same, so its callers are unaffected. `digest` and any other default-channel caller compile and behave exactly as before. The blast radius is one parameter on a shared function and one rewritten caller. The trade-off is that the `general` default stays implicit inside `post`.

Removes: the inline body construction and retry loop in `jobs/report.ts`
Adds: an optional `channel` parameter (default `"general"`) on `lib/notify.ts#post`; `jobs/report.ts` calls `post(message, channel)`; tests showing `post` sends to a supplied channel, still defaults to `general`, and still retries once
Pattern: follows the owning helper `lib/notify.ts#post`, and removes the parallel copy of it in `jobs/report.ts:2-6` instead of extending it.

**Alternative: a required channel on `post`, made explicit at every call site.** This drops the assumption that `post` should keep a default at all. Every caller names its channel, so a missing channel is a compile error rather than a quiet `general`. `report` collapses onto `post` the same way. The cost is caller blast radius. `jobs/digest.ts` must change to `post("Daily digest", "general")`, and so must every other importer of `post`, which I couldn't enumerate from these files. That makes the change's size unknown until a repo-wide search runs. It also touches callers whose behavior isn't changing at all.

Removes: the inline body construction and retry loop in `jobs/report.ts`; the hardcoded `"general"` default in `lib/notify.ts#post`
Adds: a required `channel` parameter on `lib/notify.ts#post`; explicit `"general"` at `jobs/digest.ts:2` and at every other `post` call site; `jobs/report.ts` calls `post(message, channel)`; tests for supplied-channel delivery and the unchanged retry count
Pattern: also follows `lib/notify.ts#post` as the single owner, but spreads the default-channel decision across every caller. That widens the change beyond the one caller that needs it.

**Considered but not viable:**
- **A new notification service.** You ruled it out, and the existing helper already owns the path.
- **A static per-job channel mapping.** It would drop the runtime channel `report` already receives from its callers (`jobs/report.ts:1`), so the requested channel couldn't vary per call.

I'd switch to the required-argument approach if a repo-wide search shows `digest` is the only `post` importer, or if we've had bugs from messages silently landing in `general`. Either would make explicit channels worth the extra edits.

## 1. First message to the user

The framing holds: I checked the supplied `lib/notify.ts#post`, traced the inline delivery in `jobs/report.ts#report`, and followed `jobs/digest.ts`’s message-only call; the two delivery implementations share the same formatting and two-attempt retry behavior, with no additional loader or runtime dependency involved.

The code supports consolidating report delivery into `post`: its hard-coded channel is the only behavior preventing reuse. The report already accepts a requested channel, and the digest relies on the helper’s `"general"` default. No load-bearing premise was contradicted or remains unverified in the supplied observations.

Your recorded answers keep that framing and permit either an optional channel argument or a required channel argument with explicit updates to existing callers. I’ll compare those directly, preserving retries and digest delivery to `"general"` without introducing a notification service.

## 2. Approaches message

I recommend **A: keep the default in the shared helper and add an optional channel argument**. The distinguishing axis is **who owns the default channel**: the notification helper or each caller. Neither approach needs a new service, loader, or runtime dependency; no missing or uncheckable implicit dependency was identified.

### A) Optional channel argument — default owned by the helper

Change the shared signature to `post(message: string, channel: string = "general")` and use that channel in its existing payload. Replace the report’s inline delivery implementation with `post(message, channel)`. Leave the digest’s `post("Daily digest")` unchanged.

This is the minimal reuse-only option. The nearly-fitting path is `lib/notify.ts#post`: it already owns formatting, the endpoint, and retries; it lacks only caller-selected channel support. Both jobs would use its existing two-attempt behavior, including rethrowing the second failure.

The trade-off is that an omitted channel intentionally means `"general"` rather than producing a compile-time error. In return, existing message-only callers remain compatible.

Removes: duplicated payload formatting, HTTP request, and retry loop from `jobs/report.ts#report`.
Adds: a defaulted channel parameter and channel payload binding in `lib/notify.ts#post`; a `post` import and delegated call in `jobs/report.ts`.
Pattern: consolidates delivery under the existing owning helper, `lib/notify.ts#post`, while preserving the message-only caller contract demonstrated by `jobs/digest.ts`.

### B) Required channel argument — default made explicit at callers

Change the shared signature to `post(message: string, channel: string)`. Delegate report delivery to `post(message, channel)` and update the digest to `post("Daily digest", "general")`.

This drops the assumption that the shared API must retain an implicit default, as your recorded answer permits. It still reuses the existing delivery implementation and preserves formatting and retries. Requiring a channel makes routing explicit and lets TypeScript flag omitted arguments.

Its larger caller blast radius is the cost: the digest must change despite having no new delivery requirement, and the general-channel choice moves out of the helper.

Removes: duplicated payload formatting, HTTP request, and retry loop from `jobs/report.ts#report`; the helper’s hard-coded general-channel selection.
Adds: a required channel parameter and channel payload binding in `lib/notify.ts#post`; a `post` import and delegated call in `jobs/report.ts`; an explicit `"general"` argument in `jobs/digest.ts`.
Pattern: retains centralized delivery in `lib/notify.ts#post`, but deliberately replaces the implicit-default contract used by `jobs/digest.ts` with caller-owned routing.

I would choose **B** only if compile-time enforcement of an explicit channel at every call becomes more important than preserving existing message-only calls; otherwise, **A** best meets the compatibility requirement.
